steps.text: In a large pot over medium high heat, saute the ground beef for about 5 minutes, or until browned. Drain off excess fat.
Add the tomatoes, sauce, water, vegetables, soup mix and sugar. Bring to a boil and reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Martha's Vegetable Beef Soup
raw_recipe.description: Ground beef and a package of frozen vegetables are your two main shopping list items for this quick-to-make soup. The hearty, flavorful broth is made with tomato sauce, dry onion soup mix, and a teaspoon of white sugar.
raw_recipe.name: Martha's Vegetable Beef Soup

recipeInstructions.text: In a large pot over medium high heat, saute the ground beef for about 5 minutes, or until browned. Drain off excess fat.
Add the tomatoes, sauce, water, vegetables, soup mix and sugar. Bring to a boil and reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.

review.reviewBody: This recipe was really easy and really tasty too. However, instead of using water, I substitued beef broth and added potatoes!

Thank you so much for this wonderful recipe! My husband was angry with me so after I made it and ate some I went to bed. When he got home and tasted it, he woke me up to tell me how wonderful dinner was and totally forgot that he was mad at me. He told me it was the best tasting dish that I had ever made. 
I also used 1lb of ground beef, browned it with 3 cloves of garlic and a small chopped onion. I exchanged the water for beef broth. I chopped up a green pepper and 1/3 lg box of mushroom too (to clean out the fridge)and added that to the frozen veggies (which were also chopped into smaller bites). I added 1/3 can of kidney beans and two hand fulls of ditalini. The 1/2c of red wine really topped off the stock. It was super easy to prepare and I will certainly be making it again! Thanks

So I will start by saying I have never made Beef Vegetable Soup before and honestly, I haven't eaten it much either. So I can into this not sure what it was really supposed to taste like. At my house, there are 6 so I always add extra meat. I started by using 2lbs of 80% ground beef and 1 large chopped onion and about 1 TBS of minced garlic with a bit of olive oil in my Ninja slow cooker on stove top setting. Browned all the meat, drain some of the grease but not all. I find that just gives soups a meaty flavor. 2 cans of diced tomatoes with juice in(because I hate stewed) I added 6 cups of beef broth, 2 bags of frozen veggies, 2 can of tomato sauces and 1 can of 8 oz tomato paste because I think I added a bit too much beef broth to tomato ratio (my family ended up liking it exactly like that so I will do that again) I also threw in a few beef bouillon cubes because I did not have onion mix and because I wanted a very beefy and tomato-ey flavor. For spices, I did add a bit more garlic powder because I think I went light on the minced garlic, sugar (doubled for the recipe), a dash of red pepper, a good bit of dried parsley( maybe a couple of TBS), some salt and black pepper to taste, and a TBS of Worcestershire sauce. I let it sit on high slow cook for 4 hours. At first I was a bit worried about the soup but over the time it really blossomed in a very hearty rich tasting soup. So I am sorry for completely changing the recipe, but I would not have had any idea where to start!

I love soup and this recipe appealed to me. My neighbor and I had a cook-off. She did it exactly as it appeared but I made some changes. Since I don't eat very much beef (maybe 3 or 4 times a year out or at someone's house), I used a pound of ground turkey as I doubled the recipe. Instead of just water, I used 4 cups of chicken stock. I had a 16-oz BAG of frozen mixed vegetables, and since I had 4 baby Yukons, I decided to cut them up and add them in. For the DRY onion mix soup, I used an entire envelope since there is no salt used in the recipe (It seemed silly and wasteful to only use half). Topped with some grated Parmesan cheese, this was great. My neighbor and I sampled each others soup -- I WON BIG TIME!

As some other reviewers suggested I used a pound of ground beef and sauteed with garlic and onion. Used 2 cans of stewed tomatoes and just broke them up with my hands as I was adding them. I used half low sodium beef broth and water for the liquid, and added 1 tsp Italian Seasoning, 1 tsp Crushed Red Pepper flakes, 1/2 tsp. black pepper, & 1 Bay Leaf. I let it simmer for about an hour instead of the 20 mins, but it came out really, really good! A great soup and what a dollar stretcher!

I doubled the recipe and like others I tweaked it. I used beef stewing meat cut into 1/2 in pieces or smaller. Sauteed one chopped medium onion with a teaspoon of minced garlic in olive oil for a few minutes before adding the beef. Once the beef was browned I added the rest of the ingredients substituting beef broth for the water. I also added about a tablespoon of worcester sauce, a half tsp pepper and a couple shots of hot sauce. After a delicious sampling I zip-lock bagged the remainder in 2-portion amounts for the freezer and future enjoyment.

Really tastes good and a snap to make. I added a small onion and a clove of garlic when browning the meat. Also substituted a can of beef Broth for the water. Tossed everything into me instapot (pressure cooker) and cooked for 10 minutes. By the time I took the dog out, the meal was ready. A piece of crusty bread compliments the final product. Highly recommended.

I love this because it’s so simple and perfect for a chilly night. I made it all in crock pot. I made a few adjustments, substituted beef broth for the water and added some potatoes. I also added barley after cooking for recommended time, I added another 20 min for that. It was so tasty and with a few oyster crackers, I was all set. Thanks for a new regular on my table.

I made this excellent recipe. Instead of tomato sauce I used 2 table spoons of thick and zesty tomato sauce dry mix. 3 beef bouillon cubes with a total of 3-4 cups of water. I used one whole lb. of hamburger. I cut up 5 potatoes, into cubes, and added them last. Once the potatoes finished the soup was ready to devour!!! Wonderful recipe!!! Thank you All Recipe app & also a special shout out to Martha!

This was a great soup! I used 2 cans of low sodium beef broth instead of water, chopped up a small yellow onion to brown with 1 lb of ground beef and seasoned the beef with garlic powder and pepper. All the other ingredients I left the same except I did add a 1/2 cup of Marsala wine. It was a delicious, hearty soup! Will make again!

This recipe is delicious! I doubled the recipe so I had leftovers. I used stew meat instead of groundbeef. And added some cubed potatoes. I did use Italian style stewed tomatoes & sauce. Also, instead of water I used beef broth. I definitely will be making this again!!

I loved it and my family too. I used the tip to use beef broth instead of water. I used unsalted beef broth because I knew the dry onion mix would have a high amount of salt to it. I also used canned mixed vegetables with potatoes in it. And, it worked out perfect. I will be making it again.
Love it, no changes made!

Made this for supper tonight. I did add some potato and used beef stock instead of water. I also added 2 additional cups of the stock and used a full pound of hamburger. Even the picky toddlers ate the broth and the hamburger. The rest of the family has already requested it again.
I also used beef broth. Gave alot of flavor.
So easy to make! Tastes great!

It was very easy to make, however, I feel weird saying I made exactly this. Without the tweaks, it didn't have much flavor. Didn't taste the onion soup mix at all. So, I ended up using all the ingredients, plus some beef broth, a little Ragu, added noodles, and seasonings of my choice. I'd make this again if I went with my added ingredients.
Love this recipe!! Made it today, I added sliced mushrooms, cabbage & a vadalia onion for more onion flavor.

Everyone loves it and it will go in the rotation of frequently made meals! The only changes I made were I used beef broth instead of water and I used more ground beef than it calls for. Perfect, and easy, otherwise!

We love this soup. I followed the recipe except I used Italian style stewed tomatoes because I that's what I had in the pantry. I threw in a parmesan rind just because I wanted to. Thanks Martha for sharing this recipe.
